body: Actual: +0.3% MoM vs +0.4% forecast (previous +1.4%, revised); +6.5% YoY vs +6.6% forecast. Core +0.3% MoM, in line.

What it means: the monthly number cooled, but the yearly number is still hot — +6.5% YoY is the biggest annual rise since November 2022, and core is +4.9% YoY. With a December Fed hike still priced and Treasury yields above 5%, the pressure on gold has paused, not lifted.

Gold's reaction (Kitco): spot caught a modest bid to about $3,897.90, +0.57% on the day, testing resistance at $3,900 — a bounce off Thursday's 52-week low near $3,852 after a three-session fall of about 6%.
Levels: a firm hold above $3,900 opens $3,930, then $3,950–$3,970 and $4,000. If the bounce fails, $3,870 and then the $3,852 low are exposed again.
Call: NO TRADE into the bounce — the desk's standing rule held (no manual scalps 20:15–21:30 Phnom Penh on release night). Reassess once gold either holds above $3,900 or loses $3,870.
headline: PPI cooler than expected — a relief bounce for gold, not a trend change
Logan speaks in ~10 min — hawkish stance already priced in, no trade into the speech
body: No forecast — a speech, not data. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan (2026 FOMC voter) gives opening remarks at the 2026 Bank Funding Conference.

Her stance is already known and priced in: on Tuesday she said the FOMC needs 'at least two more 25bp hikes' and the rate is ~50bp below modestly restrictive. Gold has already fallen 4%+ this week on this hawkish repricing, with the dollar at a 19-month high.
Gold ~$3,890, just under $3,900, day range ~$3,873–3,923, just above its 52-week low near $3,853. A hawkish repeat keeps it capped under $3,900.
Tonight's PPI came in a touch softer than forecast (0.3% vs 0.4% MoM) and gave gold a small bounce — but core stayed sticky, so the Fed's hawkish line hasn't cracked.
Flip: a dovish softening (pause talk) would turn it BUY toward $3,900–3,923; a 50bp December hike endorsement would turn it SELL, watch $3,873 then $3,853.
Caution: the first minutes after any headline are spike territory — no manual scalps into the speech, per the standing rule.

headline: Logan's speech was technical — no new rate signal, hawkish backdrop unchanged
body: What she said: at the Dallas Fed's Bank Funding Conference, Logan said the US Treasury market is functioning 'very well' and the Fed should strengthen its support tools, including extending discount-window operations to weekends and holidays.

No new rate-path signal: her Tuesday stance (at least two more 25bp hikes) stands unchanged. The hawkish backdrop is intact — December hike ~89–91% priced, dollar near a 19-month high, 10-year yield ~5.13%.

Gold ~$3,890–3,910, recovering modestly from Thursday's 13-month low (~$3,874) but still under the $3,900–3,910 pivot and on track for a >4% weekly loss. No source reports a specific gold move on the speech.
Levels: resistance $3,925 / $3,937 above; support $3,884 / $3,875 / $3,860 below. A break of $3,937 would change the picture.
Call: NO TRADE — nothing tradable in a technical speech, and Bowman speaks at 22:50 Phnom Penh with Daly at 00:00. No manual scalps into those prints, per the standing rule.

headline: Bowman speaks in ~13 min — same hawkish message as Tuesday, low surprise value
body: No forecast — a speech, not data. Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman speaks at 22:50 Phnom Penh.

Her last remarks were Tuesday (10 Nov) at the Council on Foreign Relations: inflation 'has persisted longer than hoped', 'still work to do' to reach 2%, core PCE ~3.3% — a hawkish lean, but she stopped short of endorsing a December hike. Tonight likely echoes that.
Gold ~$3,888–3,891, recovering slightly after Thursday's ~3% slide to a 13-month low, but still down ~4% this week. Support $3,853–3,870, resistance $3,937.
Backdrop stays hawkish: a December 25bp hike is ~85–89% priced and the dollar is near a 19-month high; today's PPI came in a touch soft (MoM 0.3% vs 0.4% forecast), giving gold only a small lift.
Flip: an explicit December hike or 50bp endorsement would turn it SELL (dollar up, gold down); a softening — hikes off the table or inflation easing — would turn it BUY.
Caution: the first minutes after a Fed speech headline are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print, per the standing rule.

headline: Bowman's speech was on supervision and regulation — no new rate signal, hawkish backdrop unchanged
body: What she said: tonight's speech was on supervision and regulation (per the Fed schedule), not the economy or rates — in line with her role as Vice Chair for Supervision. No new rate-path remarks have been reported in the wires.

Her stance is unchanged from Tuesday (10 Nov): inflation 'has persisted longer than hoped', 'still work to do' to reach 2%, core PCE ~3.3% — a hawkish lean, but she stopped short of endorsing a December hike.

What it means for gold: nothing changes. The hawkish backdrop is intact — a December 25bp hike is ~88% priced, the 10-year yield is ~5.13%, and the dollar is near a 19-month high. No source reports a gold move on the speech.
Gold ~$3,878, drifting just under $3,900 after today's small PPI bounce, still down ~4% on the week after Thursday's slide to a 13-month low near $3,853.
Levels: resistance $3,900 / $3,937 above; support $3,870 / $3,853 below. Next up: Fed's Daly speaks at 00:00 Phnom Penh — no manual scalps into that print, per the standing rule.
Call: NO TRADE — a supervision speech with no policy content is not tradable for gold.
